what: An effect that makes a sound swell and dip in volume at a steady speed.
how: A slow wave (RATE) is used as a volume control on the sound, so it gets louder and quieter over and over. DEPTH is how far the volume falls, and WAVE chooses the shape of the swell. A sine is smooth; a square switches abruptly between loud and quiet.

ins.rate: A control signal that changes the speed. Each 1.0 of signal doubles the RATE (an octave), -1.0 halves it. Patch an LFO or ENV here.

outs.out: The sound with its volume rising and falling.

knobs.rate: How fast the volume pulses, 0.1 to 20 times a second.
knobs.depth: How deep the dips go: 0 is no change, 1 drops all the way to silence.
knobs.wave: The shape of the swell: SINE (smooth), TRI (a straight up-and-down), SAW (a ramp, with one sudden change per cycle), SQUARE (on and off).

try: Patch VCO into TREMOLO's in and TREMOLO's out into OUT's left and right. Hold a note on KEYS, set RATE around 5 Hz, then switch WAVE to SQUARE for a chopped sound.
